**Title:**
Gmail Android App users on the latest Gmail Android release may experience issues accessing their inbox.
**Description:**
Our engineering team has identified the root cause and is actively working on mitigating the issue.
We will provide more information by Tuesday, 2026-09-22 18:00 PDT.
**Symptoms:**
- Users on the Gmail Android app are finding that their accounts unexpectedly appear logged out.
- Upon re-login, the process completes but the app fails to recognize the account.
- Users receive an error message stating the account is already added.
**Workaround:**
The workaround for the Gmail app issue is to uninstall recent application updates and revert to the system's base version of Gmail. Optionally reinstall the latest version of the Gmail app from play store.
Alternatively, users can access https://mail.google.com on their mobile browsers.

**Description:**
The issue with Google Drive has been resolved for all affected customers as of Wednesday, 2026-09-16 07:41 PDT.
We thank you for your patience while we worked on resolving the issue. **Customer Symptoms:**

Users were advised to retry actions.

updates.text:
# Incident Report
## Summary
On Wednesday, 16 September 2026, Google Drive experienced an issue where a subset of traffic was dropped for a duration of 39 minutes.
We sincerely apologize for the disruption this incident caused to your business. We recognize the critical role Google Cloud plays in your operations and deeply regret the impact on your services. Our engineering teams have resolved the issue and have taken immediate measures to address the incident. Additionally, engineering teams are conducting a comprehensive review of the incident to fully address the root cause and prevent the recurrence of such an event.
## Root Cause
This incident was triggered by a planned capacity test which temporarily reduced Google Drive's serving capacity.
The sequence of events leading to the impact was as follows:
Engineers initiated a routine capacity test, causing Drive to operate with reduced capacity.
The remaining available capacity was insufficient to handle peak user traffic.
As traffic exceeded capacity, the capacity protection system was triggered and began blocking legitimate Drive requests.
## Remediation and Prevention
The issue was detected on Wednesday 16 September 2026 at 7:03 via our automated outage detector systems that monitor error rates and user queries.
To mitigate the symptoms, Google engineers initiated an immediate rollback of the capacity test to restore serving capacity. Additionally, engineers upsized available capacity and updated the system load limit threshold to add more capacity headroom.
Google is committed to preventing a repeat of this issue in the future and is completing the following immediate actions:
- Resilience and Resourcing: Ensure sufficient buffer capacity is available globally during capacity tests.
- Address the Root Cause: Engineering is conducting a comprehensive review of capacity modeling and protection thresholds to ensure they correctly account for capacity tests during peak traffic periods.
## Detailed Description of Impact
On Wednesday, 16 September 2026, from 07:03 to 07:43 US/Pacific, customers were unable to access Google Drive. A subset of overall traffic to Google Drive was dropped during this window.
Affected users experienced failures, elevated latency, or timeouts when attempting to access, upload, or sync files in Google Drive.
**Additional Information for Customers:**
Customers who experienced impact during this window are encouraged to review their deployment logs. If you continue to see lingering issues beyond the incident window, please file a support ticket via the Google Workspace support portal.
